title: Cocoa banana overnight oats
description: Oats soaked overnight in milk and yogurt with cocoa, mashed banana and chia. Tastes like chocolate pudding, ready when you wake up.

steps.text: Mash one banana with a fork in a big bowl. Whisk in the cocoa, honey and a splash of the milk until smooth.
steps.tip: Mixing the cocoa with a little liquid first stops it from making dry lumps.

steps: Stir in the rest of the milk, the yogurt, oats and chia.

steps.text: Spoon into 4 jars or boxes, close them and put them in the fridge overnight, or for at least 4 hours.
steps.tip: The chia seeds swell and make it thick and creamy.

steps.text: In the morning, slice the second banana on top. Eat it cold, straight from the jar.
steps.tip: Too thick? Stir in a little milk. It keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Fluffy blueberry pancakes
description: Thick American-style pancakes dotted with berries, served with a drizzle of maple syrup. A slow weekend breakfast.
steps: Melt the butter in the frying pan you will use, then pour it into a cup.
Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a bowl. In another bowl whisk the egg, milk and melted butter.

steps.text: Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir gently with a spoon, only until there is no dry flour left.
steps.tip: A few lumps are fine. Stirring too much makes flat, tough pancakes.

steps.text: Heat the buttery pan on medium-low. Pour in small ladles of batter and scatter a few berries on each.
steps.tip: Use the berries straight from the freezer, so they do not turn the batter purple.

steps.text: Cook for about 2 minutes, until bubbles appear on top and the edges look dry, then flip and cook for 1 minute more. Repeat with the rest.
steps.tip: If they brown before the middle is cooked, turn the heat down.

steps: Serve warm in stacks with the maple syrup.

title: Potato hash with peppers, bacon and fried eggs
description: Crispy fried potato cubes with onion, pepper and bacon, topped with runny fried eggs. A hearty weekend breakfast.

steps.text: Cut the potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes, no need to peel. Boil them in salted water for 5 minutes and drain well.
steps.tip: Boiling first makes them soft inside and lets them crisp quickly in the pan.

steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan on medium-high and fry the chopped bacon for 3 minutes.

steps.text: Add the potatoes and fry for 10 minutes, turning only every few minutes, until golden and crisp.
steps.tip: Leave them alone between turns: that is how they get a crust.

steps: Add the chopped onion and pepper, the paprika and salt and fry for 5 minutes more until soft.

steps.text: Make 4 hollows in the hash, crack an egg into each, cover the pan and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the whites are set.
steps.tip: The yolks should still wobble. Leave the lid on a minute longer if you like them firm.

steps: Scatter with parsley and serve from the pan.
equipment: large frying pan with a lid

title: Banana oat cookies with raisins
description: Soft chewy cookies made from ripe bananas, oats and peanut butter, with raisins and a few chocolate drops. No flour, no added sugar.
steps: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a tray with baking paper.

steps.text: Mash the bananas well with a fork, then mix in the peanut butter and cinnamon.
steps.tip: The browner the bananas, the sweeter the cookies.

steps: Stir in the oats, raisins and chocolate drops. Leave for 5 minutes so the oats soak up the banana.

steps.text: Scoop 20 heaped spoonfuls onto the tray and flatten them a little.
steps.tip: They do not spread in the oven, so shape them how you want them.

steps.text: Bake for 15 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool on the tray: they firm up as they cool.
steps.tip: Keep them in a box for 4 days. Two cookies make one snack.

title: Apple cinnamon muffins with walnuts
description: Soft yogurt muffins full of apple pieces, cinnamon and walnuts. Good for breakfast on the go or with coffee.
steps: Heat the oven to 190 °C and put 12 paper cases in a muffin tin.
Mix the flour, sugar, baking powder and cinnamon in a big bowl.
Whisk the eggs, yogurt and oil in another bowl. Peel and dice the apples and chop the walnuts.

steps.text: Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir with a spoon only until just combined. Fold in the apples and most of the walnuts.
steps.tip: Lumpy batter makes light muffins. Smooth batter makes heavy ones.

steps: Spoon into the cases and scatter the rest of the walnuts on top.

steps.text: Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until risen and golden.
steps.tip: Done when a toothpick pushed into the middle comes out clean. They keep 3 days in a box and freeze well.

title: Roasted red pepper hummus with veg sticks
description: Smooth hummus blended with roasted peppers and paprika, with carrot and cucumber sticks for dipping.
steps: Drain the chickpeas, keeping a little of their liquid. Drain the peppers.

steps.text: Blend the chickpeas, peppers, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, paprika, salt and half the oil until very smooth, adding a spoon or two of the chickpea liquid if it is too thick.
steps.tip: Blend for a full 2 minutes. Longer blending gives creamier hummus.

steps: Spoon into a box and drizzle with the rest of the oil and a pinch of paprika.

steps.text: Cut the carrots and cucumber into sticks to dip.
steps.tip: The hummus keeps 4 days in the fridge. Cut fresh sticks each day.

title: Vanilla pudding with warm berries
description: Creamy vanilla pudding made from a packet the Croatian way, topped with berries warmed into a quick sauce.

steps.text: Whisk the pudding powder and {60 g} of the sugar with {150 ml} of the cold milk in a cup until smooth.
steps.tip: Always mix the powder with cold milk first, or it goes lumpy.

steps: Bring the rest of the milk to the boil in a pot.

steps.text: Take the pot off the heat, whisk in the pudding mix, then put it back on medium heat and stir for 1 minute until it bubbles and thickens.
steps.tip: Keep stirring and scrape the bottom so it does not burn.

steps: Pour into 6 small bowls or glasses.

steps.text: Warm the berries with the rest of the sugar in a small pan for 5 minutes until juicy. Spoon over the pudding, warm or cold.
steps.tip: Press cling film on top of the pudding if you want no skin. It keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Knedle sa šljivama (plum dumplings)
description: Soft potato dough wrapped around whole plums, boiled, then rolled in buttery toasted breadcrumbs with cinnamon sugar. A late summer favourite.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 25 minutes until soft. Peel them while warm and mash or press them until smooth. Leave to cool.
steps.tip: Cold, dry potatoes make a dough that holds together without much flour.

steps.text: Knead the potatoes with the egg, salt, {10 g} of the butter and the flour into a soft dough.
steps.tip: Add the flour bit by bit and stop as soon as it stops sticking. Too much flour makes heavy knedle.

steps: Wash the plums, cut a slit in each and take out the stone. Put a small pinch of the sugar inside each one.

steps.text: Roll the dough out 1 cm thick and cut it into squares. Wrap each square around a plum and roll it into a smooth ball between your hands, pinching it closed.
steps.tip: Any crack lets water in while boiling, so seal them well.

steps.text: Lower the knedle into a big pot of gently boiling water and cook for 10 to 12 minutes after they float up.
steps.tip: Cook them in two batches so they do not stick together.

steps: Meanwhile melt the rest of the butter in a wide pan and toast the breadcrumbs on medium for 4 minutes until golden. Mix the rest of the sugar with the cinnamon.
Lift the knedle out with a slotted spoon, roll them in the toasted breadcrumbs and serve warm, sprinkled with cinnamon sugar.
